page: Amazon Web Services t3a.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The configuration allocates 4 burstable vCPUs spanning 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 16.0 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance is provisioned with a 1 Gbps baseline network profile, does not include local disk storage, and contains no hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark measurements indicate performance characteristics oriented around sporadic rather than continuous processing loads. In compute benchmarks, the instance recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 692.0 and a multi-core score of 1674.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 3622.97 and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 1181.97. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 23.87 GB/sec, while write bandwidth yielded 11.7 GB/sec. While lacking AVX-512 and AMX instructions, onboard hardware support for AES and SHA-NI allows the processor to maintain stable cryptographic throughput, achieving 3207.35 in PassMark CPU encryption tests.

Given its shared-core burstable CPU credits, t3a.xlarge provides an economical footprint for workloads with intermittent computational requirements. The platform suits non-production environments such as staging nodes, code repositories, internal tooling, and microservices with fluctuating access patterns. It is also viable for small-scale web serving and caching backends that remain within baseline CPU envelopes, though continuous heavy compute, low-latency database queries, and sustained high I/O workloads are constrained by the burst credit model and the absence of local NVMe storage.
description: Amazon Web Services t3a.xlarge is a general-purpose, burstable cloud instance based on the Nitro hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.2 GHz, it provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, coupled with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory at a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server lacks bundled local storage and GPU hardware, operating with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations indicate entry-level compute throughput, with Geekbench scores of 692.0 in single-core and 1674.0 in multi-core, while PassMark encryption achieves 3207.35 leveraging hardware AES and SHA-NI flags. As a burstable instance, it offers cost-efficient compute density when applications run primarily at low-to-moderate baselines with occasional usage peaks. It is appropriate for staging deployments, light web backends, microservice hosting, and internal testing environments.
